goldens.comment: The rendered GrafanaRuleListItem is missing the required key prop for React list items. This can cause rendering issues when the list order changes.

RuleActionsButtons is invoked with only promRule, but SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer inside RuleActionsButtons still depends on a Grafana Ruler rule being present, so for Grafana rules coming from list views the 'Silence notifications' menu entry (now driven by Grafana Prom abilities) will toggle showSilenceDrawer without ever rendering the drawer. This means clicking 'Silence notifications' for these rules has no visible effect, even when abilities indicate silencing is allowed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/components/rule-viewer/AlertRuleMenu.tsx:165 — canDelete` now becomes true via the new `grafanaDeleteAbility` (prom-only) path, but the render guard `canDelete && rulerRule` still requires a truthy `rulerRule`; in the refactored rule-list view only `promRule` is passed (rulerRule is undefined), so the Delete menu item silently never renders even for users who have delete permission

adjudication.rationale: The diff refactors list rendering to be Prometheus-only for Grafana-managed rules (GrafanaGroupLoader now maps only `promResponse.data.groups.at(0)?.rules` and no longer fetches/uses any ruler-rule data). At the same time, `AlertRuleMenu` now computes `canDelete` as an OR of ruler-based and prom-based abilities (`rulerDeleteAbility` || `grafanaDeleteAbility`). If the menu rendering still gates the Delete item on `rulerRule` being truthy (as the finding claims: `canDelete && rulerRule`), then in the new prom-only list view `rulerRule` would be `undefined` and Delete would never render despite `grafanaDeleteAbility` allowing it. The diff does not show the actual render guard lines in `AlertRuleMenu.tsx`, so the exact condition cannot be directly verified here, but the scenario is consistent with the refactor intent and the new data flow.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/rule-list/GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx:53 — Removing the ruler query and the `matchRules` logic means rules that exist only in the Ruler (not yet propagated to Prometheus, i.e. newly created) or only removed from Ruler but still present in Prometheus no longer render "Creating"/"Deleting" placeholder states; the list now silently omits in-flight rules instead of reflecting their transitional state

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the ruler query and all `matchRules`/placeholder rendering: `GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx` no longer calls `useGetGrafanaRulerGroupQuery`, no longer computes `matches`/`promOnlyRules`, and now renders only `promResponse.data.groups.at(0)?.rules` via `GrafanaRuleListItem`. It also deletes the “Creating” branch (ruler-only rules) and the “Deleting” `RuleOperationListItem` branch (prom-only rules), and corresponding tests for those states are removed/rewritten. This means transitional states would no longer be represented if such mismatches can occur. However, the old code itself comments that Grafana Prom rules “should be strongly consistent now,” implying this omission may be an intentional tradeoff rather than a guaranteed defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/rule-list/components/RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx:68 — When `getEditableIdentifier` can't build an identifier (rule missing/not a Grafana prom rule) it only calls `logWarning` (line 146) and the component silently `return null`, hiding all rule action buttons (edit/silence/delete/duplicate) from the user with no visible error state or retry path.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `RuleActionsButtons.V2` now computes `identifier = getEditableIdentifier(...)` and immediately `return null` if it’s falsy. `getEditableIdentifier` only constructs an identifier when either a `rule` (RulerRuleDTO) is provided or when `prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(promRule)` is true; otherwise it just `logWarning(...)` and returns `undefined`. In that case, the entire actions UI disappears with no visible error/disabled state. This is a real, diff-grounded robustness/UX issue, but the diff doesn’t prove that such a call path occurs in production (the new Grafana list item passes a GrafanaPromRuleDTO, which should succeed), so it’s not clearly a verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/rule-list/GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx:1 — The entire Ruler-group reconciliation (`matchRules`, its `logWarning('...No matching Prometheus rule found for Ruler rule')`, and the Creating/Deleting placeholder rows) was deleted along with the ruler query, so if Prometheus rule data is ever out of sync with Ruler-created/deleted rules (the exact eventual-consistency case this code was written for), the rule list will now silently render fewer/missing rows with no warning logged and no in-progress indicator.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the Ruler query (`useGetGrafanaRulerGroupQuery`), the reconciliation logic (`matchRules`), the `logWarning('...No matching Prometheus rule found for Ruler rule')`, and the Creating/Deleting placeholder rows from `GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx`. The loader now renders only `promResponse.data.groups.at(0)?.rules` and only errors when `!promResponse`. Therefore, any mismatch where Ruler has rules not yet reflected in the Prometheus response (or vice versa) would no longer be detected, logged, or represented with placeholder rows. Whether that mismatch can still happen is not verifiable from the diff (it may be an intentional assumption of strong consistency), so it’s best treated as an edge-case/observability regression concern rather than a proven bug.
